name: TX-37
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
No competitive polling or expert ratings
model.rationale: The D+30 district fundamentals, Casar's roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing near 97% for Democrats all point to a safe Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at the baseline margin with modestly tightened uncertainty.
model.watch: An unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising surge or outside spending could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Casar, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second term in this Austin-based district, which leans about 30 points Democratic. He has raised more than $1.1 million and holds nearly $600,000 on hand, while Republican Lauren Peña has raised under $120,000 with almost no cash remaining and no visible outside support. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97%.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and the financial imbalance. The expected margin is roughly 29 points, consistent with the seat's partisan lean, and the race is rated Safe Democratic.
